# <span id="aanchor338"></span> Exception Resolver Widget

The FLOWCAL dashboard includes an Exception Resolver widget that displays the number of "Unresolved" and "Pending" exceptions associated with a given list.

By default, a single Exception Resolver widget displays on the dashboard, using the first list from the default system specified on the [User Preferences](../Settings%20Manager/User%20Settings/User%20Preferences.md) screen.

The Exception Resolver widget will display the exact number of exceptions up to 9,999. If the number of exceptions is 10,000 or higher, the amount will be abbreviated with a decimal (example: 10,289 exceptions will display as 10.2K).



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 555;height: 224;" />

Click the **More** link in the bottom right corner of the widget to open the [Exception Resolver](../Exceptions/Exception%20Resolver/Exception%20Resolver.md). After resolving exceptions, click the refresh button 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> to update the exception count.

When you access the Exception Resolver by clicking the More link, exceptions with a status of Pending or Unresolved will display by default. Otherwise, the Exception Resolver will display exceptions based on your user preferences or session settings.

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Change List">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Change Lists</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Change List">

You can change the list for an Exception Resolver widget directly from the dashboard.

<div class="procedure">

To change a list:

1.  Click the list name at the top of the widget. A drop-down will display the available lists.
2.  Select the desired list from the drop-down list.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 176;height: 416;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Add-Remove">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Add or Remove an Exception Resolver Widget</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Add-Remove">

You can display up to 10 Exception Resolver widgets on your dashboard.

<div class="procedure">

To add or remove a widget:

1.  Click the gear icon 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> in the top right corner of the main screen to open the Settings menu.
2.  Click **Dashboard Manager**.
3.  Click **Exceptions**.
4.  Click the "X" icon 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="icon" /> to remove the widget from your dashboard, or click the **Select to add a new widget** link to add a new widget.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," style="width: 630;height: 347;" />

</div>

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Configure">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Configure an Exception Resolver Widget</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Configure">

Use the Dashboard Manager to specify the system and list associated with an Exception Resolver widget. You can also assign specific colors to widgets to help make your data easy to view.

<div class="procedure">

To set up an Exception Resolver widget:

1.  Click the gear icon 

<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="icon" style="width: 15;height: 15;" /> in the top right corner of the main screen to open the Settings menu.
2.  Click **Dashboard Manager**.
3.  Click **Exceptions**.
4.  Add a new widget if necessary.
5.  Click the **System** and **List** fields to select a system and list for your widget. You can also begin typing in these fields to search for a name.
6.  Assign a specific color to the widget (optional).

</div>

</div>
